sources.title: TodoMVC behavior reference: precise functional contract

model.vision: A dependable todo list that a small team can start using immediately.

objectives.statement: Get a small team using the todo list for real work within one working day of delivery, with no training required.
Ensure no one loses a todo, its wording, or its done state when they close the app, restart their device, or the system restarts: zero lost items.
Reduce the effort of keeping a list tidy, so that correcting a todo never requires re-entering it and finishing or clearing many todos takes one action rather than one per todo.
Let people know how much work they have left at any moment, with the remaining count correct 100% of the time, whichever part of their list they are reviewing.
Let the organization's agent tooling and hosted workspaces do everything a person can do with a todo list, with the same results, so no second way of keeping todos has to be maintained.

model.mission: Adopt the familiar TodoMVC behavior as a fixed contract rather than inventing a new experience, so people have nothing to learn. Keep every list safely on record away from anyone's device, so people and agent tooling always work from the same list. Ship the full everyday experience working end to end, and decline anything beyond it until the team asks.

items.definition: A person who keeps their own todo list, to add tasks, check them off, and get them out of the way once finished.
The group of colleagues adopting the todo list together for real work, each User keeping their own list; sharing a list between Users is not offered.
The organization's software agents that work a User's todo list on that User's behalf, doing anything the User can do.
An organization workspace that embeds the todo list alongside its other hosted tools, so a User can work the list from inside it.
Put a new, not-yet-completed Todo at the end of the List from text the User supplies; a Blank Title adds nothing.
Change the Title of an existing Todo without removing and re-adding it; finishing with a Blank Title removes the Todo instead.
Back out of a Reword Todo in progress, leaving the original Title exactly as it was.
Take one Todo off the List, whether completed or not, leaving every other Todo untouched.
Mark one Todo as completed, or unmark it, leaving every other Todo untouched.
In one action, mark every Todo completed, or, if every Todo is already completed, mark every Todo not completed.
In one action, remove every Completed Todo from the List, leaving Active Todos untouched; does nothing when there are none.
Look at the List under a chosen Filter, always able to see which Filter is in effect, without changing any Todo.
One of three ways to review the List: All shows every Todo, Active shows only Active Todos, Completed shows only Completed Todos.
Know at a glance how many Active Todos remain, whichever Filter is in effect, with the number correct right after any action that changes it.
The number of Active Todos on the whole List, not merely the number currently being shown.
Come back after closing the app, restarting a device, or a restart of the system and find the same List, with the same Titles and completed states.
Agent Tooling or a Hosted Workspace carries out any everyday action on a User's List, with the same results as if the User had done it.
The full set of things a User can do with a List: Add Todo, Reword Todo, Abandon Reword, Remove Todo, Toggle Todo, Toggle All, Clear Completed, Review List, See Items Left, and Return to List.

The well-known reference behavior for a todo list, adopted as the fixed contract for the Everyday Experience; due dates, priorities, tags, sharing, reordering, undo history, and offline working are outside it.
Judging whether supplied text is empty or only whitespace, and therefore cannot be a Title.
Deciding whether a finished Reword Todo changes the Title or, because the new text is a Blank Title, removes the Todo.
Deciding which way Toggle All goes: not completed when every Todo is already completed, otherwise completed, including when the List is mixed.
Deciding which Todos belong under the Filter in effect, based only on their completed state.
Working out Items Left from the completed states of every Todo on the List, regardless of the Filter in effect.
Enter one new Todo at the end of a User's List in the List Record.
Replace the Title of one Todo in the List Record.
Set whether one Todo is completed in the List Record.
Set every Todo on a User's List to the same completed state in the List Record, as one action.
Remove one Todo from the List Record.
Remove every Completed Todo on a User's List from the List Record, as one action.
Retrieve a User's whole List, with its order, Titles, and completed states, from the List Record.
The durable record, held away from anyone's device, of every User's List; it survives closing the app, a device restart, and a system restart.
The ordered collection of Todos kept for one User.
One task on a List, made up of a Title and whether it is completed.
The free-text wording of a Todo, never a Blank Title.
Text that is empty or contains only whitespace, which is never kept as a Title.
A Todo not yet completed; still left to do.
A Todo marked as completed; done, and eligible for Clear Completed.

model.rationale: recommend DecompressedSolution: lowest in-band composite risk (0.325) at 140.0 days (App C risk-crossover exclusions applied)

items.name: Interface-protocol volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the protocols through which software reaches the todo capabilities, today an ordinary web API and MCP. WHY: the agent-facing protocol is young and still moving. LONGEVITY GROUNDING: MCP has shipped several dated specification revisions per year since its late-2024 release, and agent tooling conventions are moving with it; at that rate multiple breaking or reshaping revisions fall inside even a 1-year horizon, and web API conventions shift more slowly but within 3-5 years. LIKELIHOOD: high for the agent protocol, moderate for the web API. EFFECT: if protocol shapes reach into the list actions, each revision ripples through every action and risks people and agents getting different results, breaking Objective 5. Source: founder brief, 'reachable both as an ordinary web API and as an MCP surface'; Mission Objective 5.

items.name: Durable-record technology volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the technology and arrangement holding the List Record away from anyone's device. WHY: the brief fixes the outcome (a real service that survives restarts) and leaves the mechanism open, and the app starts as something a team will 'try out', so the volume and criticality it must carry will move if it sticks. LONGEVITY GROUNDING: storage choices for small services are typically revisited every few years as hosting, volume and house standards change, which falls within a 3-5 year horizon if the trial becomes lasting use; this rate is an architect's judgement, not a measured figure. LIKELIHOOD: low within the trial, moderate over 3-5 years. EFFECT: every record and recall path would change, and a botched change directly threatens Objective 2's zero lost items, so the cost is high even though the change is infrequent. Source: founder brief, 'not a toy that only lives in the browser's memory'; TodoMVC reference section 9; Mission Objective 2.

items.name: Hosting-platform volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the organization's house way of running services: gateway, execution substrate, deployment target and capacity arrangements. WHY: the brief binds the system to 'the way we build everything else here', so the system inherits every change to that standard on the organization's schedule, not its own; the platform doctrine itself anticipates its execution substrate being replaced. Agent tooling can also drive load far above what a small team of people generates, which moves capacity arrangements. LONGEVITY GROUNDING: organizational platform standards are typically revised every few years, inside a 3-5 year horizon; this rate is an architect's judgement, not a measured figure. LIKELIHOOD: moderate over 3 years. EFFECT: unencapsulated, runtime and hosting specifics spread through every service and a platform change becomes a rewrite. Source: founder brief, 'built the way we build everything else here'; mission carry-forward constraint 1; platform runtime doctrine entry 1.

items.name: Presentation-host volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the host a person sees and works the List in, and what that host allows. WHY: two hosts must work at once, an ordinary web app and an embedded Hosted Workspace surface, and they differ in layout, input gestures and what the host controls; the brief also leaves the screens open. LIKELIHOOD: certain today, since both ship at first delivery, and more hosts are likely as the organization adds hosted tools. EFFECT: if the Everyday Experience is bound to one host, the second becomes a parallel implementation, which is exactly the 'second way of keeping todos' Objective 5 rules out, and the behaviors drift apart. Traces pending: no Required Behaviors exist on this branch yet. Source: founder brief, 'an ordinary web app, plus an MCP Apps surface'; TodoMVC reference sections 2 and 7, whose gestures are examples ('e.g.'); Mission Objective 5.

items.name: Caller-identity volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: how the system establishes whose List a request is for, and on whose authority it acts. WHY: callers establish this differently at the same time: a person in a web app, a person inside a Hosted Workspace, and Agent Tooling acting for a User. The reference describes only a 'single user/session', while the brief and glossary require each member of a Small Team to keep their own List, and how they are told apart remains unsettled. LIKELIHOOD: certain today, because three caller kinds ship together; further change is likely as the organization's sign-in and agent-delegation practices evolve. EFFECT: identity logic embedded in actions or surfaces would ripple through all of them on any change, and an error here shows one User another's List. Traces pending: no Required Behaviors exist on this branch yet. Source: founder brief, 'our team', 'our other agent tooling'; TodoMVC reference preamble; open question in the Mission draft notes; Glossary terms Small Team, Agent Tooling, Work List on Behalf.

items.name: Change-propagation volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: how a change made by one caller reaches another caller already looking at the same List. WHY: the reference assumes one user in one session, but the Mission puts people and Agent Tooling on the same List, so an agent can change it while a person has it open. The available means differ by caller at the same time: a web app, an embedded host and an agent client do not share one way of being told about changes. LIKELIHOOD: high from first delivery, as soon as an agent works a List a person has open. EFFECT: Items Left and the shown Todos go stale on an open screen, breaking Objective 4's 'correct 100% of the time'; retrofitting a mechanism touches the surfaces and the service together. Traces pending: no Required Behaviors exist on this branch yet. Source: TodoMVC reference section 8, 'live count', 'updates immediately'; Mission Objectives 4 and 5, 'always work from the same list'.

items.name: Todo-attribute volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: what a Todo carries beyond its Title and completed state. WHY: the reference says 'at minimum' a title and a flag, the brief leaves the item's shape open, and the Mission declines additions only 'until the team asks', which expects requests to come; due dates, priorities and tags are the usual first ones. This entry does not put any of them in scope: it only keeps a new attribute from being expensive when asked for. LIKELIHOOD: moderate to high within 1-3 years if the team adopts the app for real work. EFFECT: the item's shape runs through the List Record, both protocols and every presentation host, so one new attribute would touch all of them unencapsulated. Traces pending: no Required Behaviors exist on this branch yet. Source: TodoMVC reference preamble and out-of-scope list; founder brief, 'leaving the exact shape of the todo item ... up to you'; Mission statement.

rejected.name: Everyday-behavior rules volatility
rejected.reason: The Mission adopts TodoMVC Behavior as a fixed contract and the reference notes many apps implement it identically; add, reword, remove, toggle and clear will not change unless the product stops being this product.

rejected.name: Toggle-All direction volatility
rejected.reason: The reference pins all three cases (all done, none done, mixed); this rule is the contract itself and has no open-ended variation to insulate.

rejected.name: Items-Left counting volatility
rejected.reason: The count of not-completed Todos across the whole List is fully defined by the reference and is arithmetic over the completed state; no realistic change is in view.

rejected.name: Review-filter set volatility
rejected.reason: A further way to review the List would be one more predicate over stored Todos, added in one place with no ripple beyond a new option on each surface.

rejected.name: Blank-title definition volatility
rejected.reason: What counts as blank (for example, which whitespace characters) is a single check that a small conditional handles.

rejected.name: Reword-commit gesture volatility
rejected.reason: Enter, losing focus, Escape and double-click are the reference's examples of how a host expresses Reword and Abandon Reword; they vary by host, so they are the same change as Presentation-host volatility.

rejected.name: Frontend-framework volatility
rejected.reason: Replacing the web app's framework changes how one presentation host is built, not anything below it; insulated by the same boundary as Presentation-host volatility.

rejected.name: Agent-tool vocabulary volatility
rejected.reason: How agent tools are named and described moves with agent protocol conventions; it is the same underlying change as Interface-protocol volatility.

rejected.name: Web-API versioning volatility
rejected.reason: Evolving the web API's shape is the slower half of the change Interface-protocol volatility already covers; a separate entry would split one boundary in two.

rejected.name: Sign-in provider volatility
rejected.reason: Which provider signs a person in is one instance of how the caller is established, so it belongs to Caller-identity volatility.

rejected.name: Agent-delegation permission volatility
rejected.reason: Objective 5 grants agents everything a person can do, so no per-agent permission rules are required today; on whose authority an agent acts is already part of Caller-identity volatility.

rejected.name: Capacity and load volatility
rejected.reason: Agent-driven load changes capacity arrangements, and those are met by how the service is hosted, not by a seam in the todo actions; covered by Hosting-platform volatility.

rejected.name: Execution-substrate volatility
rejected.reason: The durable execution runtime is part of the house platform this system inherits, so it changes with Hosting-platform volatility on the organization's schedule.

rejected.name: Backup and recovery approach volatility
rejected.reason: How the List Record is protected against loss is decided with the technology holding it, so it moves with Durable-record technology volatility.

rejected.name: Shared-list volatility
rejected.reason: The reference excludes multi-user sharing and the Glossary gives each User their own List; shared lists would add ownership and conflict rules for a business the brief does not describe.

rejected.name: Reordering volatility
rejected.reason: Drag-to-reorder is excluded by name and new Todos always go at the end; nothing in the research shows anyone asking for another order.

rejected.name: Undo-history volatility
rejected.reason: Undo/redo is excluded by name, and Abandon Reword and un-toggling already cover the corrections the brief asks for.

rejected.name: Offline-working volatility
rejected.reason: Offline sync is excluded by name and conflicts with the Mission's single List Record held away from devices; supporting it would change the product's basic promise.

rejected.name: Reminders and notifications volatility
rejected.reason: No source mentions alerting anyone; a transport seam here would insulate a feature nobody has requested.

rejected.name: Reporting and analytics block
rejected.reason: A reflex block with no business driver: the only figure anyone asks for is Items Left, which the Everyday Experience already provides.

rejected.name: Logging and audit block
rejected.reason: A reflex block: no source asks for a history of actions or an audit requirement, and undo history is excluded.

rejected.name: Multi-organization tenancy volatility
rejected.reason: The brief describes one organization's team; separating organizations would design for a hypothetical hosted-product business.

rejected.name: Language and locale volatility
rejected.reason: The audience is one internal team and no source mentions other languages or regions; Titles are already free text.

rejected.name: Regulatory retention volatility
rejected.reason: No source mentions regulated data or retention duties for a team's todo items, and Objective 2 concerns not losing items rather than a legal retention period.

Hosting-platform volatility is deliberately not crossed by this flow or any other: no business step depends on how the service is run. It is exercised by the Deployment and Operations Model.

decisions.essenceRationale: Every User and every agent, on every host, needs the same thing from this product: a List that stays correct as they change it, under one set of rules, kept on one record. That need outlasts every change of screen, protocol, storage or Todo shape, and it would hold even if every gesture were redrawn. It is what separates this product from the demo it is modelled on, where the list lives and dies in one browser, and from a second way of keeping todos that drifts from the first. It is an abstraction: the customer never asked to 'tend' anything, yet add, reword, remove, toggle, toggle all and clear completed are all this one behavior differing only in how the change resolves.

nodes.label: Capture which Filter the caller wants on the caller's surface, whichever host or protocol it arrives through
Establish whose List is wanted and on whose authority the caller acts
May this caller see this List?
The caller is told the request was refused; nothing of the List is shown
Recall the User's whole List from the List Record

Work out Items Left across the whole List, regardless of the Filter
The caller's surface shows the matching Todos, the Filter in effect and Items Left; no Todo changes
An open view stays correct because Tend the List makes each change known; a caller told of a change takes stock again.

decisions.essenceRationale: Everyone who keeps a List keeps it in order to know what is left, and that question does not change whichever User, agent or host asks it, or however the List is stored. Trusting the answer is what makes the List worth keeping: the Todos found must be the ones recorded, even after a restart, and the count must be true for the whole List rather than for what happens to be shown. This is a behavior distinct from Tend the List because it never changes a Todo. It is an abstraction: reviewing under a Filter, seeing Items Left and coming back to the List are one act of reading the record, differing only in what prompted it and how much is shown.

verdicts.summary:
REVISE. The layers, cardinality, dynamic-view coverage, RA-to-Resource labels and note use are sound, and the draft changed no slot other than the System. Five defects need fixing. Items 1 and 2 turn the drafter's own flags 2 and 3 into required changes.

1. Volatility ownership: Change-propagation volatility. ListManager and ChangeNoticeAccess both claim it in encapsulatesVolatilities, with no ratified facet group. Remove it from ListManager's typed list and prose, leaving ChangeNoticeAccess as sole owner. The 'sequence' half is not volatile: every changing path announces after recording, and only the means varies by caller kind. Keep the shared claim only if a reviewer ratifies it as a facet pair and that ratification is recorded.

2. Notification obligation with no receiving seam: ChangeNoticeAccess -> ChangeNoticeChannel, 'signal callers with this List open'. Nothing in the model connects the channel to any Client. No Client claims this volatility, and Take Stock's free note n12 ('a caller told of a change takes stock again') relies on a hop nobody can trigger. As drawn, it also reads as a Resource publishing to Clients, which the don'ts forbid. The gap is recorded only in a commit message, which is not a disposition on the draft. Doctrine rules out broker pub/sub, so do not fix this with a Pub/Sub Utility. Closed layering forbids upward calls but not a Client calling down and waiting, for example a watch operation on ListManager that consults ChangeNoticeAccess. Such an edge has no activity node to realize it, so do not add it to the System alone: DV-REL-COVERAGE would fire, and a fabricated step is worse. Required: (a) escalate a .coreUseCases amendment that gives the receive path a node, then draw it; or, if that cannot happen in this job, (b) state the deferral on ChangeNoticeAccess's Encapsulates prose, naming the receive path as unresolved and owned by .operationalConcepts, and reword the channel edge label so it claims only what the model does. Under (b), also say in the draft that Objective 4 remains unproven for an open screen.

3. Same Manager operation realized differently (symmetry and realization truth). Compare the fragments for Tend the List n6/n9, Drive n5/n6 and Hosted Workspace n4/n6 with the per-operation views:
- removeTodo: recallList + ResolveChange + strikeTodo in the first three, but only strikeTodo in 'Remove a todo' n4.
- toggleTodo: recallList + ResolveChange + recordCompletedState in the first three, but only recordCompletedState in 'Mark a todo done or not done' n4.
- addTodo: recallList + ResolveChange in the first three, but CheckTitle(text) with no recall in 'Add a todo' n4.
- rewordTodo: ResolveChange in the first three, but ResolveReword(wording) with no recall in 'Fix a todo's wording' n4.
- clearCompleted: no-effect is decided from ResolveChange before the write in the first three, but from removedCount after the write in 'Sweep away finished todos' n4/n5.
These are the same operations on one Manager, so at most one drawing is true per operation. ResolveChange reads as a gross-terms placeholder for work the variations draw differently. It also claims agents and workspaces take a different path from people on the same operation, which is what Objective 5 rules out. Decide what each operation actually does, then make the core and the variations agree. Name the real Engine operations in the family fragments, or draw the consultation in the variations. If that exposes a mismatch in a committed activity diagram, escalate it rather than bending a fragment.

4. takeStock drawn without its match: 'Drive the list from agent tooling' n8/n10. The n2 entry includes takeStock and n11 promises 'the same result a person would have seen', yet the read branch is recallList then CountItemsLeft, with no MatchFilter. Take Stock n7 and Come back n5 both call MatchFilter for this operation. Add MatchFilter(list, filter) to the n8 fragment after the recall.

5. Todo-attribute volatility is not actually contained: ListRecordAccess.atomicBusinessVerbs recordNewWording and recordCompletedState/recordCompletedStateForAll. ListResolvingEngine claims this volatility 'over a Todo as a whole', and Tend n19 says a new attribute has 'one path to travel'. But these RA verbs and their fragments (recordNewWording(listOwner, todoId, title), recordCompletedState(listOwner, todoId, completed)) name individual attributes, so a due date would add RA verbs and ripple through the Manager. Reshape the RA verbs so a change keeps the Todo as a whole. Keep the atomic all-at-once and strike verbs, avoid Insert/Update-shaped names, and update every fragment and static label that cites the old verbs.

NOTED, NOT BLOCKING (do not reopen these):
- WebApp/WorkspaceApp and WebApi/McpServer each share one volatility across per-host Clients. Accepted: each Client is one instance of the host or protocol.
- ListManager carrying Hosting-platform volatility with a stated deferral is accepted (flag 1), given doctrine's limit on the substrate. After item 1 it is ListManager's only typed volatility. That follows from the committed list having no workflow volatility, and the Manager is not a pass-through because it really orchestrates.
- Single-surface 'Work the list from a hosted workspace' and User-only variations drawing two of four surfaces are justified by their actors.
- 'Abandon a reword' having no Manager call is honest.
- The recall in Drive n6 (flag 6) is accepted because the diagram has no recall node on that path.
- reviewList and seeItemsLeft ride only the human edges, while agents get the same content through takeStock. Acceptable, but revisit if contract design finds them redundant.
- Add n5, Fix n5, Toggle All n5, Tend n7 and Workspace n5 turn on an Engine verdict and lack decidedBy. Add it when .coreUseCases is next amended.
- 'Remove a todo' and 'Mark a todo done' have no already-removed branch, though Tend n8 names that case. Raise this with any amendment from items 2 or 3.
- For .operationalConcepts: reconcile IdentityProvider with gateway authentication (flag 4).
- The ListManager name is a domain-flavoured noun, but it is not one-for-one with use cases. No change required.

verdicts.summary:
REVISE. The two core picks are sound and I am not asking to change them: Tend the List and Take Stock of the List subsume all ten everyday behaviors in the brief and TodoMVC reference, and the essence rationales are real arguments. Three defects need fixing.

1. CHANNEL-SHAPED USE CASES (required). Remove "Drive the list from agent tooling" and "Work the list from a hosted workspace" as separate use cases. Their own rejection reasons say so: "A different caller, not a different behavior" and "A different host, not a different behavior". Channels are permutations of one behavior, never separate use cases, even as nonCore entries. In the customer's words, the brief lists these under "the delivery side", not among what a user does. Each one also redraws the core flow as a thinner copy with no refusal branch, and the agent entry can only link to Tend the List although it also reads, which your commit message admits. Tend the List already carries what they add: Agent Tooling is a declared actor, and n2 says "whichever host or protocol it arrives through". Keep Objective 5 visible on the cores. In particular, n3 (Establish whose List...) should cover what a Hosted Workspace vouches for, and the same step in Take Stock should do likewise, since that detail would otherwise be lost when the hosted entry goes.

2. LANES DO NOT RESOLVE TO DECLARED ACTORS (required). The "Caller" lane appears on both cores and on all 10 remaining variations, but no use case declares a "Caller" actor. They declare User and/or Agent Tooling. "Caller" is also not a Glossary term. The "Hosted Workspace" lane on the hosted variation has the same defect and goes away with item 1. "Todo System" as a non-actor system lane is fine. Fix: on the User-only variations, lane the caller-side nodes "User". On the two cores, either draw a lane per declared actor (separate start entries are legal) or declare one actor role that the lane names, as long as the lane resolves. Also retry the actor link your commit message reports as lost: linkedActorId is null on every node, and the stored field is linkedActorId against actor ids such as "user". If the tool still drops it, say so in the draft rather than leaving it silent.

3. "Switch between all, active and done" contradicts its core and Objective 4 (required). Take Stock always returns Items Left, and the reference (section 8) and Objective 4 require the count to be correct whichever Filter is selected. This variation's flow never works out Items Left, and its closing note shows only the Todos and the Filter. Its rejection reason, "the read is the same", is therefore untrue as drawn. Add the Items Left step and show the count in the closing note, as "Come back to the list" already does.

ACCEPTED, NOT BLOCKING (no action needed to pass this critique):
- Refusal and not-on-record branches appear only on the cores. I accept this as your stated decision.
- Todo-attribute volatility is covered by note n19 and Hosting-platform by the justification in n20. Both are acceptable. The other five volatilities are crossed by real steps.
- The cores split along "changes the List" and "reads the List". That is close to a write/read split, but Objectives 3 and 4 back it as two things customers actually want, so it stands.
- "Make the change known to every other caller" is not literally in the brief. It is justified by Objectives 4 and 5, but keep it to the need. The mission declines extras, so it must not grow into a live-collaboration feature.
- Take Stock n6 to n7 (Recall, then Match) and "Fix a todo's wording" n4 to n5 are close to the padding shapes your doctrine warns about. Keep them only if the architecture can realize each step honestly.
- "Tend the List" and "Take Stock of the List" are understandable but not yet Glossary terms. Add them in a Glossary amendment.

GAP OUTSIDE THIS ARTIFACT: .scrubbedRequirements does not exist and no predecessor slot is committed, so this critique was made against the uncommitted Mission, Glossary and Volatilities drafts plus the research corpus. I checked the variations against the corpus directly, and no everyday behavior is missing. A redraft of this artifact cannot close this gap, so it is not a reason for this verdict, but it must be resolved before these use cases are treated as final.

changeNoticeAccess.title: changenotice contract

ChangeID.description: Identifies one logical change to the List. Issued by the caller and stable across retries of that change. Non-empty; opaque to this component.

ListOwner.description: The User whose List changed. The Glossary keeps one List per User, so this names the List. Non-empty; opaque to this component.

changeNoticeAccess.notes:
DESIGN STATE: complete, pending architect review. Do not construct against this until that review clears.

FACET: making it known that a named List has changed, to callers with that List open. Knows nothing of Todos, Filters or use-case sequence.

OPERATION AnnounceListChanged(listOwner, changeID) -> error. Precondition: both arguments non-empty, and the change is already on record. Postcondition on nil: the signal for this changeID has been accepted by ChangeNoticeChannel for callers with this List open. Sole caller: ListManager, sync (committed System edge). Called from tend-the-list n13, add-a-todo n8, fix-a-todo-s-wording n10, remove-a-todo n6, mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done n6, mark-everything-done-or-undo-that n10, sweep-away-finished-todos n7, drive-the-list-from-agent-tooling n7, work-the-list-from-a-hosted-workspace n8. No events published and no queued operations (ResourceAccess layer rule). No Temporal: ListManager wraps this call in its own Activity.

IDEMPOTENCY: keyed on changeID. Repeating a call with the same changeID returns nil and emits no second signal. Record of the changeID and emission of the signal are one atomic step, so a crash cannot record without signalling or signal without recording.

ERROR MODEL: invalid argument (empty listOwner or changeID) is TERMINAL, do not retry. Channel unreachable, timed out or otherwise unavailable is TRANSIENT, safe to retry with the same changeID. Advisory orchestration: 2s timeout per attempt, a small bounded number of retries. ListManager chooses the actual policy at its call site.

SIGNAL CONTENT: listOwner and changeID only, never Titles, Todos, counts or other List content. A receiver must take stock again through ListManager, so the authority check in take-stock (n3, n4) still applies. A signal for one List must reach only callers with that List open.

DESIGN DECISIONS ON THE REQUIREMENTS-PHASE OPEN QUESTIONS. Q2 change id: supplied by ListManager, because an id minted here could not recognize a retry as the same change. This adds changeID beyond the committed label announceListChanged(listOwner); ListRecordAccess already needs a change id for the same change, so ListManager should use one value for both. Q4 acting caller: not excluded, and no originator is passed. The acting caller may be signalled and harmlessly take stock again. Q6 content: as above. Q3 signalling failure: this contract reports the error and does not decide what it means for the user's action. Recommendation to ListManager: because the change is already on record, a failed announcement should not fail the caller's action.

INFRA: Postgres, proposed under review. Slot 6 (Deployment and Operations Model) is not committed and ChangeNoticeChannel names no technology. Postgres is on the approved menu and allows a unique changeID insert plus NOTIFY in one transaction, which gives the atomic idempotency above. The technology stays behind this contract: nothing in the signature depends on it.

OPEN FOR ARCHITECT REVIEW. (1) BLOCKING: the committed System has no path from ChangeNoticeChannel to any Client and no way to register that a List is open, so a signal has no consumer, and take-stock n12 assumes the caller is told. This contract cannot add a receive or registration op, because TP-OP-REACHED rejects an op no dynamic view calls. Fixing it needs a System amendment, after which this contract gets a revision. (2) Agent tooling: whether an agent caller holds a List open is undefined (Q7), and this is part of the same amendment. (3) Reconcile the System label to announceListChanged(listOwner, changeID). (4) Confirm sync treatment and Postgres when slot 6 is committed (Q5, Q8). No numeric latency bar is committed for this step.

FACTORING: one contract, one op. Rejected: GetOpenCallers (property-like, leaks channel state), per-caller-kind notify ops (leak the means this component exists to hide), and unsubscribe or registration ops (no dynamic view calls them).

REUSE: another team implementing this facet on a different channel would keep the signature unchanged.

APP C SECTION 6 CHECK. 1 reusable: PASS. 2a at least 2 ops: WAIVED, one op. The committed component has exactly one atomic business verb and TP-OP-REACHED forbids any uncalled op; the likely second op is the receive or registration path in open item 1, so the architect must rule on this waiver with that item. 2b 3-5 ops: WAIVED for the same reason. 2c at most 12: PASS. 2d under 20: PASS. 3 no property-like ops: PASS. 4 at most 2 contracts: PASS, one. 5 not a junior hand-off: PASS, designed in the senior-developer role, default hand-off. 6 architect or senior designer: PASS on the same basis, reviewer system-architect, review pending.

change-notice-access.content:
# ChangeNoticeAccess: requirements scope note

ResourceAccess component. It encapsulates Change-propagation volatility in the means: how a List change is made known, however each caller kind is told. Its one committed business verb is announceListChanged. ListManager holds the other half of this volatility, the sequence.

Basis: committed System (slot 5), Core Use Cases (slot 4), Volatilities (slot 3), Glossary (slot 1), Mission (slot 0). The Deployment & Operations Model and the Required Behaviors are not committed on this branch, so the sync/queued and pub/sub treatment below comes only from the System's edges, and nothing here traces to a B-NN id.

## Responsibilities

1. Accept the announcement that a named List has changed. Edge: list-manager -> change-notice-access (sync), announceListChanged(listOwner).
2. Signal the callers that have that List open. Edge: change-notice-access -> change-notice-channel (sync), 'signal callers with this List open (idempotency: change id)'.
3. Keep that signalling idempotent per change, as the same edge requires: one change is one signal, even if the signalling is attempted more than once.
4. Own the means. Everything specific to ChangeNoticeChannel, and to how each caller kind is reached, stays behind this component, so a change in those means does not reach ListManager. Source: the component's encapsulates statement and Change-propagation volatility.

The same step appears in every view that changes a List: tend-the-list (n13), add-a-todo (n8), fix-a-todo-s-wording (n10), remove-a-todo (n6), mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done (n6), mark-everything-done-or-undo-that (n10), sweep-away-finished-todos (n7), drive-the-list-from-agent-tooling (n7), work-the-list-from-a-hosted-workspace (n8). It is one obligation with one meaning, not nine.

## Out of scope

- Deciding when a change is announced. ListManager sequences this, after the change is safely on record and the changed List recalled (tend-the-list n9, n10, n12, then n13).
- Holding, recalling or counting the List. Those belong to ListRecordAccess and ListResolvingEngine. A caller told of a change takes stock again through ListManager (take-stock n12), so correctness of Items Left does not rest on the notice's content.
- Establishing who a caller is or what it may see. That belongs to IdentityAccess.
- Presenting a change on a surface. That belongs to the Clients.
- Reminders or alerts to people who do not have the List open. Rejected as speculative in the Volatilities (Reminders and notifications).

## Callers and consumers

- Sole caller: ListManager, synchronously, in the same use-case flow as the change. No other component has an edge into this one.
- Sole downstream: the ChangeNoticeChannel Resource, synchronously.
- Ultimate audience: every other caller with this List open, across WebApp, WorkspaceApp and agent tooling, which do not share one way of being told (Change-propagation volatility). The System has no edge from the channel to any Client; see open question 1.
- Schedule: the network has C-list-manager depending on this activity, so ListManager is built against this component.

## Non-functional constraints

Maintainability
- Stays ignorant of Todos, Filters and use-case sequence. It knows a List changed, not what changed or why.
- Exposes business vocabulary, not channel vocabulary, per the ResourceAccess layer rule and the committed verb.

Extensibility
- A new caller kind, or a change in how one is told, must be absorbed here and in the Resource, without touching ListManager. Presentation hosts and agent protocols are both expected to change (Presentation-host and Interface-protocol volatility).
- No growth toward shared lists, offline sync or notifications; each was rejected as speculative.

Security
- A signal for one User's List must reach only callers with that List open. The Glossary keeps each List for one User and offers no sharing, and Caller-identity volatility names one User seeing another's List as the failure to prevent.
- A signal must not become a way around the authority check. Seeing List content stays behind ListManager's check in take-stock (n3, n4).

Reliability and correctness
- Objective 4 requires Items Left to be correct 100% of the time, and the take-stock use case relies on the notice to keep an open view correct. A lost signal therefore leaves an open screen stale.
- Objective 2 requires zero lost items. By the time of the announcement the change is already on record (tend-the-list n10 precedes n13), so a signalling failure must not read as a lost change; see open question 3.
- Interactive latency: the announcement is a sync step inside the caller's own request, so it adds to that request's time. The research says the count updates 'immediately' for the acting caller, and no numeric bar is committed for this component.

## Scope of the work (beyond coding)

- Learning curve: the means for a browser host, an embedded Hosted Workspace and an agent client each differ, and the agent protocol is moving quickly.
- Integration points: ListManager and ChangeNoticeChannel only.
- Test clients: the test work must be able to observe signals as an open caller would, including across two different Lists.

## Open questions for Detailed Design

1. How does a signal reach a Client? The System ends at change-notice-channel, and no relationship or dynamic-view edge shows any Client, WebApi or McpServer receiving from it, or registering that a List is open. Take-stock n12 assumes the caller is told. The architect needs to settle this: without a path, the means this component encapsulates has no consumer in the committed design. Adding an edge is not in this activity's scope.
2. Where does the change id come from? The channel edge names it as the idempotency key, but the inbound edge carries only listOwner. It must either be supplied by ListManager or arise here, and which one determines whether a retried announcement can actually be recognized as the same change.
3. What happens when signalling fails? Tend-the-list has no failure branch at n13: the flow continues directly to the merge (n14). The change is already on record, so the likely reading is that failure must not fail the caller's action, but no committed artifact says so, nor what recovers a stale open view.
4. Who excludes the acting caller? The use-case node says 'every other caller'; the channel edge says 'callers with this List open'; and the inbound edge does not identify the originator. Either the acting caller is also signalled and harmlessly takes stock again, or something must identify it.
5. Sync or queued? Every edge here is committed as sync, but the Deployment & Operations Model that should confirm the sync/queued and pub/sub treatment is not committed on this branch. Reaching several open callers inside the acting caller's request has a latency cost, so confirm the treatment before design relies on it.
6. Does a signal carry anything beyond 'this List changed'? The use cases only need a prompt to take stock again. Confirm that no List content travels on the channel, since this affects the security constraint above.
7. Does the agent-tooling caller receive signals at all? Change-propagation volatility says agent clients are told differently, while WebApi and McpServer have only inbound edges to ListManager. Whether an agent caller holds a List 'open' is undefined.
8. ChangeNoticeChannel has an empty encapsulates statement and no named technology. Provisioning and technology choice sit outside this component, but Detailed Design needs them settled to know what it wraps.
